obligation: Chemical Facility Anti-Terrorism Standards (CFATS) incl. RBPS 8 Cyber
basis: CFATS reaches a chemical facility, an establishment that possesses or plans to possess a chemical of interest (6 CFR 27.105). Every order is drop-shipped from a supplier's plant or terminal to the customer, and no chemicals are ever at the home office, so the business has no such establishment. CFATS authority also lapsed on 2023-07-28. RBPS (a)(5), (a)(6), (a)(8) and (a)(15)-(16) are used as a voluntary benchmark because hydrogen peroxide's theft and diversion risk fits the business

obligation: USCG Cybersecurity in the Marine Transportation System rule
basis: Applicability is by MTSA facility, vessel or OCS facility status (33 CFR 101.605). The business has a home office only, and every load moves by road from the supplier's dock

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
basis: No final rule. As proposed, the size criterion is the SBA standard for the entity's NAICS code, 175 employees for NAICS 424690 (13 CFR 121.201); the business has no employees

obligation: DOT Hazardous Materials Regulations: applicability (offeror and hazmat employee)
basis: For each drop shipment the owner determines the hazard class from the SDS, prepares the BOL with the hazmat description and shipper's certification, provides the emergency response information, and books the carrier. Those are pre-transportation functions (171.1(b)), so the business is an offeror (171.8). The supplier is also an offeror for the functions it performs (171.2(b)). The owner is treated as a self-employed hazmat employee (author interpretation of 171.8, applied conservatively)

obligation: DOT HMR: hazmat registration and recordkeeping
basis: Cargo tank loads of hydrogen peroxide of about 4,000 gallons (bulk packaging of 3,500 gallons or more) and placarded quantities of the Class 8 and Division 5.1 products (107.601(a)(4) and (a)(6))

obligation: DOT HMR: shipping papers
basis: The owner prepares each BOL with the hazmat description and signs the shipper's certification

obligation: DOT HMR: emergency response information
basis: Each hazmat BOL needs an emergency response telephone number that is monitored while the material is in transportation; the business uses an ERI provider under 172.604(b)(2)

obligation: DOT HMR: hazmat employee training
basis: The owner performs hazmat functions as a self-employed hazmat employee (see HMR-171)

obligation: DOT HMR: security plan and security training
basis: About 6 cargo tank loads a year of UN2014, hydrogen peroxide 50%, Division 5.1, PG II, each above 3,000 L in a single packaging, are a large bulk quantity of a Division 5.1 PG II material (172.800(b)(10)). There is no size exemption; 172.800(c) excepts only certain farmers

obligation: DOT immediate notice and written hazmat incident report
basis: The duty falls on each person in physical possession of the hazmat during transportation (the carrier). The business never takes possession

obligation: EPA Risk Management Program
basis: Part 68 applies to owners or operators of a stationary source (68.10(a)), and 68.3 excludes transportation, including storage incident to transportation. The business holds no inventory

obligation: OSHA Process Safety Management
basis: PSM needs a process and employees. The business has neither

obligation: DEA listed chemicals
basis: The product line has no List I or List II chemical (hydrochloric acid, sulfuric acid and potassium permanganate are listed; none is sold)

obligation: Export Administration Regulations
basis: Domestic sales only

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (data security, disposal and breach notice)
basis: "Covered entity" names a sole proprietorship (501.171(1)(b)). Carrier emails with driver names and license numbers are kept in the email suite, so 501.171(2) (reasonable security), (3) to (6) (breach notice) and (8) (disposal) apply

obligation: Other states' breach notification laws
applies: Only for affected drivers who live outside Florida
basis: Carriers send driver details from Florida and other states; residence is checked at the time of a breach

obligation: FAR safeguarding and supply chain clauses
basis: The business has no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: SEC cybersecurity disclosure rules
basis: The business is a sole proprietorship, not a public company

obligation: HIPAA Security, Privacy and Breach Notification Rules
basis: The business is not a health care provider, health plan or clearinghouse (45 CFR 160.103) and holds no health information

obligation: State AI laws on consequential decisions
citation: State statutes (Colorado SB26-189, California CPPA ADMT rules, Texas HB 149)
basis: The AI assistant makes no decision about a person; the business sells only in Florida and south Georgia

obligation: FTC Act Section 5 (unfair or deceptive practices)
basis: The business makes no claims about AI to customers

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC ransomware advisory (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
applies: Yes (only if a ransom payment is considered)
basis: Applies to any U.S. person considering a ransomware payment
